sowhat.text: The AI-led selloff hits the sector driving much of the megadeal and financing activity. Fixed-ratio stock deals like Marvell and Lumentum keep their ratio but are worth less in dollars, and a VIX at 28 could slow IPOs and new bond launches until volatility settles.

pitch: Thursday was a rout. The S&P 500 fell 4.4 percent to about 7,354, the Nasdaq dropped 5.5 percent into a correction, and the Dow lost 3.4 percent, all the worst days since April 2025. The trigger was fear that Democratic wins in the midterms could bring limits on AI data centers, and Micron, AMD and Nvidia fell hard. The VIX jumped to 28. Treasuries rallied, with the 10-year down 6 basis points to 4.84 percent, and odds of a December Fed hike fell to about 67 percent. On deals, Marvell's roughly 115 billion dollar stock purchase of Lumentum is the big one, and the selloff matters for stock-funded deals.

quiz.q: How much did the S&P 500 fall on Thursday 5 Nov?
Why did the Nasdaq fall 5.5% on Thursday 5 Nov?
quiz.a: Investors feared a slowdown in AI data-center buildout, including possible moratoriums, after Democratic midterm wins. Chip and AI names such as Micron, AMD and Nvidia fell sharply.

quiz.q: Who advised Lumentum on its sale to Marvell?
quiz.a: Citi and Evercore advised Lumentum. Qatalyst, J.P. Morgan and Goldman Sachs advised Marvell.

chat.a: Thursday was a rout: the S&P 500 fell 4.4% to 7,354, the Nasdaq 5.5% into a correction, and the Dow 3.4%. AI and chip stocks led on fears of data-center limits after the midterms, and the VIX jumped to 28.2. The 10-year eased to 4.84%.
chat.tip: Lead with the AI data-center fear, then the rates.

chat.q: What's your read on oil this week?
chat.a: WTI settled at $90.52 and Brent at $98.29, both up after Wednesday's big drop. I did not find a clear reason for Thursday's rebound. Oil is volatile, so energy cash flows and upstream deal appetite hinge on where it holds.
chat.tip: Be honest about what you don't know.

chat.a: Marvell is buying Lumentum for about $115B in stock, a ~24% premium, with Qatalyst, J.P. Morgan and Goldman on Marvell and Citi and Evercore on Lumentum. Blackstone and Canadian pensions are also paying $3.1B for 49.9% of Mitsubishi's holding company that owns a stake in LNG Canada.
chat.tip: Name the advisers; bankers will ask.

chat.q: What are you watching this week?
chat.a: Friday's October jobs report, about +59K expected with unemployment at 4.2%, because it feeds the odds of a December hike, about 67% now. Then CPI on Tuesday 10 Nov. I'm also watching whether the AI selloff continues, since the VIX is at 28.2.
chat.tip: Tie each event to the Fed or the AI theme.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: The 10-year is 4.84% now. A 50 bp rise lifts the risk-free rate and so the WACC, which lowers the present value of cash flows. Companies with most of their value in the terminal value, like growth tech, fall the most.
chat.tip: Say the direction, then who is hit hardest.

chat.q: How does a tech selloff affect a stock-funded deal like Marvell and Lumentum?
chat.a: Marvell is paying 4.5 of its shares per Lumentum share, a ~24% premium to 28 Oct prices. The ratio is fixed, so a falling Marvell share price cuts the dollar value Lumentum holders receive, while the premium is measured against old prices. Boards often face pressure to revisit terms or add protections if the gap widens.

chat.q: How do the Fed and the 10-year affect M&A financing right now?
chat.a: The Fed target is 3.75–4.00% after a 25 bp hike in September, and the market puts about 67% on another on 9 Dec. The 10-year is 4.84%, so debt is costly. High yield spreads were 332 bp on 4 Nov, before the selloff, so credit's reaction is not yet visible.
chat.tip: Separate the base rate from the credit spread.
